THE ODUYA FAMILY REVOCABLE LIVING TRUST

DECLARATION OF TRUST

This Declaration of Trust is made on May 18, 2026, by Adaeze Chinelo Oduya and Farrukh Rasulov Oduya, husband and wife, of Multnomah County, Oregon, as Settlors and as initial Trustees.

ARTICLE ONE — CREATION OF THE TRUST

1.1 Name. This trust shall be known as the Oduya Family Revocable Living Trust dated May 18, 2026 (the "Trust").

1.2 Trust Property. The Settlors transfer to the Trustees the property listed on Schedule A attached to this Declaration, and the Trustees acknowledge receipt of that property. The Settlors may add property to the Trust at any time by transferring it to the Trustees, by beneficiary designation, or by will.

1.3 Character of Property. Property transferred to the Trust retains its character as community property, separate property, or joint property as it was held immediately before the transfer, and the Trustees shall account for it accordingly.

ARTICLE TWO — REVOCATION AND AMENDMENT

2.1 Reserved Power. Each Settlor reserves the right, at any time during that Settlor's lifetime and while that Settlor has capacity, to revoke this Trust in whole or in part and to amend any of its provisions, by a writing signed by that Settlor and delivered to the Trustees. On revocation, the Trustees shall deliver the affected property to the revoking Settlor.

2.2 Effect of a Settlor's Death. On the death of the first Settlor to die, this Trust becomes irrevocable as to that Settlor's separate property and that Settlor's one-half interest in any community property. The surviving Settlor retains the power to revoke and amend as to the surviving Settlor's own property.

ARTICLE THREE — ADMINISTRATION DURING THE SETTLORS' LIFETIMES

3.1 Distributions. During the joint lifetimes of the Settlors, the Trustees shall pay to or apply for the benefit of the Settlors so much of the net income and principal of the Trust as the Settlors direct, and in the absence of direction, so much as the Trustees determine is necessary for the Settlors' health, education, maintenance, and support.

3.2 Incapacity of a Trustee. If a Trustee becomes unable to manage the Trust's affairs, that Trustee shall cease to serve. Incapacity is established by the written certification of two licensed physicians, at least one of whom is a physician who has examined the Trustee within the preceding sixty days, or by a court of competent jurisdiction. The Settlors authorize the disclosure of protected health information to the successor Trustee for this purpose, and this paragraph is intended to be a valid authorization under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164.

ARTICLE FOUR — DISTRIBUTION AFTER THE DEATH OF BOTH SETTLORS

4.1 Payment of Expenses. After the death of the survivor of the Settlors, the Trustees may pay the last illness and funeral expenses of the deceased Settlor, the expenses of administering the Trust, and any death taxes payable by reason of the Settlor's death, from the Trust property, without apportionment.

4.2 Specific Distributions. The Trustees shall distribute the residence located at 3241 NE Hazelfern Place, Portland, Oregon, to the Settlors' daughter Ngozi Oduya-Rasulova if she survives the survivor of the Settlors, and the Settlors' collection of West African textiles to the Portland Art Museum.

4.3 Residue in Trust for the Children. The Trustees shall divide the remaining Trust property into equal shares, one for each of the Settlors' then-living children and one for the then-living descendants, collectively, of each deceased child. Each share is held in a separate trust on the terms of Section 4.4.

4.4 Separate Trusts. The Trustees shall pay to or apply for the benefit of each beneficiary so much of the net income and principal of that beneficiary's separate trust as the Trustees determine is necessary for the beneficiary's health, education, maintenance, and support, taking into account the beneficiary's other resources known to the Trustees. Each beneficiary may withdraw one-third of the principal at age thirty, one-half of the remaining principal at age thirty-five, and the balance at age forty. If a beneficiary dies before complete distribution, the remaining principal passes to that beneficiary's then-living descendants by representation, and if none, to the other separate trusts in proportion to their then-remaining values.

ARTICLE FIVE — TRUSTEES

5.1 Successor Trustees. On the death, resignation, or incapacity of a Trustee, the other Settlor shall serve as sole Trustee. On the death, resignation, or incapacity of both Settlors, the Settlors' son Chidi Oduya-Rasulov shall serve as successor Trustee, and if he is unable or unwilling to serve, Cascadia Fiduciary Services, Inc. shall serve.

5.2 Powers. The Trustees have all powers conferred on trustees by the Oregon Uniform Trust Code, ORS Chapter 130, and by the Oregon Uniform Trustees' Powers Act, including the power to retain, sell, lease, mortgage, and exchange property; to invest and reinvest under the Oregon Uniform Prudent Investor Act, ORS 130.750 to 130.775; to borrow; to employ counsel, accountants, and investment advisors and to pay their reasonable compensation from the Trust; to make tax elections; and to distribute in cash or in kind.

5.3 Bond and Compensation. No Trustee is required to give bond or other security in any jurisdiction. A Trustee who is not a Settlor is entitled to reasonable compensation for services and to reimbursement of expenses properly incurred.

5.4 Exculpation. No Trustee is liable for any act or omission taken in good faith and in the honest belief that it was in the best interests of the beneficiaries, except for that Trustee's own bad faith, gross negligence, or reckless indifference to the purposes of the Trust or the interests of the beneficiaries. This Section does not relieve a Trustee of the duty to act in good faith, which may not be eliminated.

5.5 Accountings. The Trustees shall furnish an annual accounting to each beneficiary then entitled to receive or eligible to receive distributions of income, and to any beneficiary who requests one in writing.

ARTICLE SIX — GENERAL PROVISIONS

6.1 Spendthrift. No interest of any beneficiary in the income or principal of the Trust may be voluntarily or involuntarily transferred, assigned, pledged, or encumbered before the Trustees actually distribute it, and no such interest is subject to the claims of any creditor of that beneficiary. This Section does not restrict a Settlor's power to revoke or amend, and it does not apply to a Settlor's own beneficial interest during that Settlor's lifetime.

6.2 Perpetuities. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, every trust created under this Declaration shall terminate no later than twenty-one years after the death of the last survivor of the Settlors and the Settlors' descendants living on the date this Declaration is signed, and the Trustees shall then distribute the remaining property to the persons then entitled to the income.

6.3 Governing Law. The validity, construction, and administration of this Trust are governed by the laws of the State of Oregon, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. The Trustees may change the situs of the Trust and the governing law to any jurisdiction in which a Trustee is qualified to act, if the change is in the best interests of the beneficiaries.

6.4 Definitions. "Descendants" means lawful descendants of all degrees, including adopted persons and persons born of assisted reproduction who are treated as children under Oregon law, and excluding stepchildren not legally adopted. "Education" means any program of study at an accredited institution, including undergraduate, graduate, professional, and vocational programs, together with reasonable living expenses.

6.5 Severability. If any provision of this Declaration is held invalid, the remaining provisions continue in effect.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Settlors and Trustees have signed this Declaration of Trust on the date first written above.

/s/ Adaeze Chinelo Oduya
Adaeze Chinelo Oduya, Settlor and Trustee

/s/ Farrukh Rasulov Oduya
Farrukh Rasulov Oduya, Settlor and Trustee

STATE OF OREGON, COUNTY OF MULTNOMAH

This instrument was acknowledged before me on May 18, 2026, by Adaeze Chinelo Oduya and Farrukh Rasulov Oduya.

Beatriz Salgado-Klein, Notary Public
